6a91ae6d32e78ede45c1171f.name: Celsius To Fahrenheit Conversion
6a91ae6d32e78ede45c1171f.description: Construct a program that computes the Fahrenheit equivalent of an input Celsius value using the formula F = (9/5)C + 32. The input Celsius value is an integer.
6a91ae6d32e78ede45c1171f.code:
#Step 1: Assign initial values to the variables which we need for this program
base = 32
conversion_factor = 9 / 5
#Step 2: Read the input Celsius value
text = input("Enter the Celsius value: ")
celsius_temp = int(text)
#Step 3: Compute the  Fahrenheit equivalent of the Celsius value
fahrenheit_temp = celsius_temp * conversion_factor + base
print("Celsius Temperature:" , celsius_temp)
print("Fahrenheit Equivalent:" , fahrenheit_temp)

6a91ae6d32e78ede45c11719.name: Determining When to Buy a New Phone (Case 2)
6a91ae6d32e78ede45c11719.description:
Construct a program that determines whether it is time to buy a new phone based on the inputs that it receives from the user. A new phone should be bought in either of the following cases:
the phone breaks
the screen has a problem
the phone has the random shutdown problem
6a91ae6d32e78ede45c11719.code:
#Step 1: Read the user input for determining whether the phone is broken 
text = input("Enter 1 if the phone is broken, otherwise enter 0:")
input_num = int(text)
#Step 2: Determine whether the phone is broken
if input_num == 1 :
    is_broken = True
else:
    is_broken = False
#Step 3: Read the user input for determining whether the phone screen is good 
text = input("Enter 1 if the phone screen is good, otherwise enter 0:")
input_num = int(text)
#Step 4: Determine whether the phone screen is good
if input_num == 1 :
    screen_is_good = True
else:
    screen_is_good = False
#Step 5: Read the user input for determining whether the phone has random shutdown problem 
text = input("Enter 1 if the phone has the random shutdown problem, otherwise enter 0:")
input_num = int(text)
#Step 6: Determine whether the phone has random shutdown problem
if input_num == 1 :
    random_shutdown = True
else:
    random_shutdown = False
#Step 7: Write the boolean expression to determine whether it is time to buy a new phone
need_phone = is_broken or not screen_is_good or random_shutdown
#Step 8: Print the result
if need_phone == True :
    print("Yes! It is time to buy a new phone.")
else:
    print("No! It is not yet the time to buy a new phone.")

Best practices: make the prompt as clear as possible (you might add a trailing space), validate the input before converting, and handle conversion errors with try/except or a loop that re-prompts until the user gives 0 or 1.

Note about Python versions: this code assumes Python 3. In Python 2, input() behaves differently (it tries to evaluate what you type), so you would use raw_input() there — but for modern code use Python 3's input().

6a91ae6d32e78ede45c11711.description: Construct a program that reads a series of temperatures and reports the days that are above 32 degrees Fahrenheit. Assume that the temperature values are in Fahrenheit. Also assume that input values could have a decimal point.
6a91ae6d32e78ede45c11711.code:
#Step 1: Read the number of days that we have to enter their temperature data

    val = float(input("Enter the temperature: "))
    temps.append(val)

    if temps[i] > 32:
        days_above_32.append("Day " + str(i+1))

6a91ae6d32e78ede45c11717.name: Determining When to Buy a New Phone (Case 1)
6a91ae6d32e78ede45c11717.description: Construct a program that determines whether it is time to buy a new phone based on the inputs that it receives from the user. A new phone should be bought if the phone breaks or the phone is at least 3 years old.
6a91ae6d32e78ede45c11717.code:
#Step 1: Read the user inputs
text = input("Enter the phone age in years:")
phone_age = int(text)
text = input("Enter 1 if the phone is broken, otherwise enter 0:")
input_num = int(text)
#Step 2: Determine whether the phone is broken
if input_num == 1 :
    is_broken = True
else:
    is_broken = False
#Step 3: Write the boolean expression to determine whether it is time to buy a new phone
need_phone = is_broken or phone_age >= 3
#Step 4: Print the result

    print("Yes! It is time to buy a new phone.")
else:
    print("No! It is not yet the time to buy a new phone.")

6a91ae6e32e78ede45c11727.name: Calculating the Employee's Wage Based on the Hours That the Employee Has Worked and an Hourly Pay Rate
6a91ae6e32e78ede45c11727.description: Construct a program for the payment department of a company to calculate the wage of an employee based on the number of hours that the employee has worked. If an employee works over 40 hours in a week, the payment amount should take into account the overtime hours. The overtime hours are paid at a rate one and a half times the regular pay rate.
6a91ae6e32e78ede45c11727.code:
#Step 1: Assign initial values to the variables which we need for this program
rate = 8.25 
standard = 40 
#Step 2: Read the number of hours that the employee has worked
text = input("Enter the number of hours that the employee has worked: ")
hours = int(text)
#Step 3: Pay overtime at "time and a half" of the regular rate of pay
if hours > standard : 
    wage = standard * rate + ( hours - standard ) * ( rate * 1.5 )
else :
    wage = hours * rate
#Step 4: Print the calculated wage
print("Wage:", wage)

How it contributes: This single value is used in both the regular-pay and overtime-pay calculations (regular hours × rate and overtime hours × rate × 1.5), so setting it correctly is crucial for correct wage results.

5.content: text = input("Enter the number of hours that the employee has worked: ")
commentList: This line displays a message to the user and reads what they type; input(...) shows the prompt and returns the user's response as a string, which you store in the variable text.

Breakdown: input("Enter the number of hours that the employee has worked: ") is a function call that prints the prompt and captures the typed text; the = operator assigns that returned string to text. The prompt must be enclosed in quotes and passed as the function argument.

Common errors/misconceptions: input always returns a string. If the user types non-numeric characters or a decimal like 40.5, the later int(text) on line 6 will raise a ValueError. Empty input or extra spaces can also cause conversion problems.

Best practices: you should validate and clean the input before converting — for example use text = text.strip(), check the content, or perform the conversion inside a try/except block. If you expect fractional hours, plan to use float(text) instead of int(text).
Naming tip: consider a clearer name such as hours_str or hours_input so you (and others reading the code) immediately know this variable holds the raw user input.

Environment note: this line waits for interactive input. In non-interactive environments (automated tests, some IDEs) input may hang or fail, so ensure the program is run where user input is supported.

7.content: #Step 3: Pay overtime at "time and a half" of the regular rate of pay

commentList: Purpose: This line checks whether the employee worked more than the standard 40 hours so you can calculate overtime pay in the following indented block (Line 9). If the condition is false, the program will go to the else block (Line 11) to compute regular pay.

Syntax and meaning: 'if' starts a conditional. 'hours > standard' uses the '>' operator to test if hours is strictly greater than standard. The trailing ':' ends the header and tells Python that the next indented lines belong to this if branch.

Potential errors and misconceptions: If 'hours' is a string (for example, if you forgot to convert input to int/float) this comparison can raise a TypeError or behave unexpectedly. Also note that '>' excludes the case hours == standard; if you wanted to treat exactly 40 hours as overtime, you would use '>=' instead.

Best practices: Make sure 'hours' and 'standard' are numeric (use int or float). Keep readable spacing ('hours > standard'). Consider allowing fractional hours by converting input with float() instead of int(), and consider validating that hours is not negative before this check.

Flow and indentation: The colon is required and the wage calculation that applies when the condition is true must be indented under this line. The corresponding else must be aligned with this if to form a correct if/else block.

9.content: wage = standard * rate + ( hours - standard ) * ( rate * 1.5 )
commentList: What this line does for you: it calculates the total pay when the employee works more than the standard hours by paying the first 40 hours at the regular rate and the extra hours at time-and-a-half.

Breakdown of the expression for you: standard * rate is the pay for the regular 40 hours; (hours - standard) is the number of overtime hours; (rate * 1.5) is the overtime hourly rate; the two parts are added to get the full wage.

Why the parentheses matter for you: they make sure you first compute the overtime hours (hours - standard) and the overtime rate (rate * 1.5), then multiply them together before adding to the regular pay.

Common mistake to avoid for you: do not compute hours * rate and then add the overtime pay on top of that, because that double-counts the first 40 hours. You must pay only the first 40 at the regular rate, not all hours.

Type and input caution for you: hours was converted with int(text) earlier, so partial hours are dropped. If you want fractional hours, use float(text) and ensure rate is a float. Also be ready to handle non-numeric input (ValueError) before this line runs.

Indentation and placement note for you: this line must stay indented under the if hours > standard: branch; if it is not indented correctly Python will raise an IndentationError or run the wrong branch.
Edge cases for you: when hours == standard this line is skipped (correct), but you should check for negative or nonsensical hours earlier and handle them explicitly.

Best-practice suggestions for you: use clearer names like regular_hours and hourly_rate, keep the parentheses for readability, and when printing the final wage format it to two decimal places to show cents.

commentList: Purpose: The else line marks the alternate branch of the if statement so that when the condition (hours > standard) is false, the program runs the code under this else — here you handle the normal (non-overtime) pay case.

Syntax and structure: In Python you write else: followed by an indented block. The colon (:) ends the else header and the indented lines below belong to this else branch. The else must be aligned with its matching if.

Semantics detail: The else branch runs when the if condition is not true — that includes hours equal to standard and any value less than standard. So the wage calculation under else covers 40 hours and fewer.

Common mistakes to watch for: forgetting the colon (SyntaxError), wrong indentation of else or its block (IndentationError), or placing else without a matching if. Also note that writing a space before the colon (else :) is accepted by Python but is non-idiomatic.

Potential misunderstanding: else does not only mean "no overtime" semantically; it runs for every case where the if condition is false. If you need to handle invalid input (like negative hours) differently, you should add a separate check before this if/else.
Best practices: keep else aligned with the if, use else: (no extra space) to follow style guides, and consider validating input first so you know the else truly represents valid non-overtime hours.

distractors.description: You might pick this line if you confuse which side should trigger the overtime calculation (thinking "less than" means special handling). If you use this line, the program will apply the overtime formula when the employee worked fewer than the standard hours. Because the overtime term uses (hours - standard), that value will be negative for these cases, which subtracts from the base pay and produces an incorrectly low wage. For example, if hours = 30, the code would compute a base of standard * rate and then add (30 - 40) * (rate * 1.5), reducing the wage incorrectly. This option inverts the intended condition: instead of checking for extra hours that deserve extra pay, it mistakenly treats short weeks as the special case and yields wrong numeric results.

You might choose this if you think the overtime branch should run only when the worked hours match the standard exactly. If you use this line, only a person who worked exactly the standard number of hours will follow the overtime calculation; employees who actually worked more than the standard will not get the overtime branch. That means people with 41, 45, or 50 hours will be placed in the other branch and paid as if they had no overtime, causing underpayment. For example, with hours = 45 the overtime won't be applied and the program will just multiply 45 by the regular rate, missing the extra 1.5× pay for overtime hours.

You might pick this line if you confuse the two variables and compare hours to the hourly pay rate. If you use this line, the condition will be true whenever the number of hours worked exceeds the pay rate (for example, hours > 8.25). That makes the overtime branch run for most typical work weeks (e.g., 9, 20, 30 hours), even though those are not overtime. As a result, the program often applies the overtime formula inappropriately, producing incorrect wages (including negative adjustments when hours are less than the standard but greater than the rate). This choice misuses the pay-rate variable as a threshold and fails to correctly identify when an employee has actually worked extra hours beyond the standard workweek.

6a91ae6e32e78ede45c11729.name: Calculating the Wage of an Employee at the Customer Service Call Center
6a91ae6e32e78ede45c11729.description: Construct a program for the payment department of a company to calculate the wage of an employee who works at the customer service call center. Like other employees in the company, the employees at the customer service call center are paid based on the hours that they work. If they work over 40 hours in a week, the payment amount should take into account the overtime hours. The overtime hours are paid at a rate one and a half times the regular pay rate.\nThe company's policy is to pay more to those employees at the customer service call center who work during weekends. Therefore, the minimum extra pay that the employees could receive for each day of work during weekends is $30. The extra pay increases to the maximum of $50 for the employees who have at least 5 days of work during weekends.
6a91ae6e32e78ede45c11729.code:
#Step 1: Assign initial values to the variables which we need for this program
rate = 8.25 
standard = 40 
weekend_pay_min = 30 
weekend_pay_max = 50 
#Step 2: Read the input data
text = input("Enter the number of hours that the employee has worked: ")
hours = int(text)
text = input("Enter the number of days that the employee has worked during weekends: ")
no_weekend_days = int(text)
#Step 3: Pay overtime at "time and a half" of the regular rate of pay
if hours > standard :
    wage = standard * rate + ( hours-standard ) * ( rate * 1.5 )
else :
    wage = hours * rate
#Step 4: Take into account the extra pay for the work during weekends days
if no_weekend_days < 5 :
    wage += (no_weekend_days * weekend_pay_min)
else :
    wage += (no_weekend_days * weekend_pay_max)
#Step 5: Print the calculated wage
print("Wage:", wage)

details.description:
Assume that we have a 7x4 matrix that stores the number of medals that seven countries won in the skating competitions at the Winter Olympic. This matrix looks like as follows:
[[ "Canada", 1, 0, 1 ],
 [ "China", 1, 1, 0 ],
 ...]
Each row of this matrix corresponds to the medal counts for the country in that row. The second, third, and fourth numbers within a row represent the number of Gold, Silver, and Bronze medals won by the corresponding country in that row.
Construct a program that takes this matrix and prints a table of medal counts with row and column totals. The column totals are the sum of the gold, silver, and bronze medals won in the competition. The output table should look like as follows:
      Country    Gold  Silver  Bronze   Total
         Canada        1       0       1          2
            China        1       1       0          2
           ...
Column Total      4       4       4

details.name: Finding the Smallest Divisor of a Positive Number
details.description: Construct a program that finds the smallest divisor (other than 1) of a positive number. For example, the smallest divisor of 4 is 2.

details.name: Finding the Largest Divisor of a Positive Number
details.description: Construct a program that finds the largest divisor of a positive number, excluding the number itself. For example, the largest divisor of 24 is 12.

details.name: Receiving Input Integers Until a Certain Condition is Met (Case 1)
details.description: Construct a program that receives an integer from the user, outputs that integer, and stops receiving integers when the user enters a negative integer.

details.name: Receiving Input Integers Until a Certain Condition is Met (Case 2)
details.description: Construct a program that receives an integer from the user, outputs that integer, and stops receiving integers when the user enters an integer that is not in the range of 30 to 90 both inclusive.

details.name: Receiving Input Integers Until a Certain Condition is Met (Case 3)
details.description: Construct a program that receives an integer from the user, outputs that integer, and stops receiving integers when the user enters a negative integer or an integer greater than 1000.

details.name: Receiving Input Integers Until a Certain Condition is Met (Case 4)
details.description: Construct a program that receives an integer from the user, outputs that integer, and stops receiving integers when the user enters an even integer less than 10.

details.name: Calculating Body Mass Index (BMI)
details.description:
BMI is a measure of body fat based on height and weight that applies to adult men and women. BMI Categories are as follows:
Underweight = <18.5
Normal weight = 18.5–24.9
Overweight = 25–29.9
Obesity = BMI of 30 or greater.
English BMI Formula (Imperial) is: BMI = (Weight in Pounds / (Height in inches x Height in inches)) x 703.
Construct a program that calculates the Body Mass Index (BMI) according to this formula.

details.name: Calculating and Rounding Up Body Mass Index (BMI) To the Nearest Integer
details.description:
BMI is a measure of body fat based on height and weight that applies to adult men and women. BMI Categories are as follows: 
Underweight = <18.5
Normal weight = 18.5–24.9
Overweight = 25–29.9
Obesity = BMI of 30 or greater.
English BMI Formula (Imperial) is: BMI = (Weight in Pounds / (Height in inches x Height in inches)) x 703.
 BMI results are usually displayed as integers (values without decimal points). Construct a program to round the BMI result to the nearest integer.

details.name: Warning the User about the Changes in the Temperature
details.description: Construct a program that receives the temperature for today and yesterday and warns the user when it is getting colder or warmer or neither. The temperature values could have a decimal point.

details.name: Warning the User about the Changes in the Temperature and Humidity
details.description: Construct a program that receives the temperature and humidity for today and yesterday and warns the user when it is getting colder or warmer or neither. When it is getting warmer, the program should also warn the user about the changes in humidity. In particular, it should warn the user when today's humidity is more, less, or has not changed compared to yesterday's humidity. Note that the temperature and humidity values could have a decimal point.

details.name: Add Values to an Empty List (Case 1)
details.description: Construct a program that creates a list of first ten positive odd numbers.

details.name: Add Values to an Empty List (Case 2)
details.description: Construct a program that creates a list of eight string values received from the user.

details.name: The Class for Representing a Loan (Case 1)
details.description: Construct a class that represents a loan. This class should contain data representing the interest rate, loan amount, and the length of loan period (in years); all of which could be accessed or changed only through the getter and setter methods. An instance of the class should be created by specifying annual interest rate, length of loan period, and loan amount.\nThe other method of the this class should calculate the amount of monthly payments on the loan.

details.name: The Class for Representing a Loan (Case 2)
details.description: Construct a class that represents a loan. This class should contain data representing the interest rate, loan amount, and the length of loan period (in years); all of which could be accessed or changed only through the getter and setter methods. An instance of the class should be created by specifying annual interest rate, length of loan period, and loan amount.\nThe other methods of the this class should calculate the amount of monthly payments on the loan as well as the total payment.

details.name: Determining the Weather Condition (Case 1)
details.description: Construct a program that determines whether it is both too hot and too dry based on the inputs that it receives from the user.

details.name: Determining the Weather Condition (Case 2)
details.description: Construct a program that determines whether it is either too hot or too dry (or both) based on the inputs that it receives from the user.

details.name: Determining the Weather Condition (Case 3)
details.description: Construct a program that determines whether it is too hot but not too dry based on the inputs that it receives from the user.

details.name: Determining the Weather Condition (Case 4)
details.description: Construct a program that determines whether it is either too hot or too dry but not both based on the inputs that it receives from the user.

details.name: Finding Adjacent Duplicates in a Sequence of Numbers
details.description: Construct a program that checks whether a sequence of numbers, entered one at a time, contains adjacent duplicates. The user enters -1 to indicate the end of the input.\nFor example, 4 is a duplicate in the sequence of numbers 1, 3, 4, 4, -1.

details.name: Finding Adjacent Consecutive Numbers in a Sequence of Integers
details.description: Construct a program that checks whether a sequence of integers, entered one at a time, contains adjacent integers that are consecutive. The user enters -1 to indicate the end of the input.\nNote that integers which follow each other in order, without gaps, from smallest to largest are consecutive numbers. For example, 12, 13, 14 and 15 are consecutive numbers.

details.name: Finding Adjacent Numbers in Ascending Order in a Sequence of Numbers
details.description: Construct a program that checks whether a sequence of non-zero numbers, entered one at a time, contains adjacent numbers in ascending order. Numbers are said to be in ascending order when they are arranged from the smallest to the largest number. For example, 5, 9, 13, 17 and 21 are arranged in ascending order.\nNote that you need to think what value should the program use to indicate the end of the input.

details.name: Modifying a List (Case 1)
details.description: Construct a program that increments all values of the list by 1.

details.name: Modifying a List (Case 2)
details.description: Construct a program that swaps pairs of adjacent elements of the list. For example, if the list is [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], the program will change it to [2, 1, 4, 3, 6, 5].\nThis program assumes that the list has always an even number of elements.

details.name: Finding the Number of Days Above the Average Temperature
details.description: Construct a program that reads a series of temperatures and reports the average temperature and the number of the days that are above the average. Assume that the input values could have a decimal point.

details.name: Displaying the Days That are Above 32 Degrees Fahrenheit
details.description: Construct a program that reads a series of temperatures and reports the days that are above 32 degrees Fahrenheit. Assume that the temperature values are in Fahrenheit. Also assume that input values could have a decimal point.

details.name: Printing the Squares of Numbers Within a Specified Range (Case 1)
details.description: Construct a program to write out the squares of even positive integers less than or equal to 10.

details.name: Printing the Squares of Numbers Within a Specified Range (Case 2)
details.description: Construct a program to write out the squares of odd positive integers less than 10.

details.name: Printing the Squares of Numbers Within a Specified Range (Case 3)
details.description: Construct a program to write out the squares of every number between 20 and 25, both inclusive.

details.name: Determining When a Student Fails a Course (Case 1)
details.description: Construct a program to determine whether a student fails the course based on the inputs that it receives from the instructor. The student fails the course if the exam score is less than 55 or student has more than 2 missing homework.

details.name: Determining When a Student Fails a Course (Case 2)
details.description: Construct a program that determines whether a student fails the course based on the inputs that it receives from the instructor. The student fails the course if the exam score is less than 55 or when the student has cheated.

details.name: Determining When a Student Fails a Course (Case 3)
details.description: Construct a program that determines whether a student fails the course based on the inputs that it receives from the instructor. The student fails the course if his/her score is not above the class average.

details.name: Determining When to Buy a New Phone (Case 1)
details.description: Construct a program that determines whether it is time to buy a new phone based on the inputs that it receives from the user. A new phone should be bought if the phone breaks or the phone is at least 3 years old.

details.name: Determining When to Buy a New Phone (Case 2)
details.description:
Construct a program that determines whether it is time to buy a new phone based on the inputs that it receives from the user. A new phone should be bought in either of the following cases:
the phone breaks
the screen has a problem
the phone has the random shutdown problem

details.name: Creating a Dictionary of Character-Count Pairs
details.description:
Construct a program that has a function which receives a string from the user and creates a dictionary that maps each character in the given string to its frequency, that is, how many times that character appears in the given string.
For example, if the given string is "book", the program creates the following dictionary:
b : 1
o : 2
k : 1

details.name: Creating a Dictionary of Character-Words Pairs
details.description:
Construct a program that has a function which receives a string and creates a dictionary that maps each character to the list of distinct words in the given string that start with that character. The dictionary should be case insensitive.
For example, if the given string is "This is my test score", the program creates the following dictionary:
t : ['this', 'test']
i : ['is']
m : ['my']
s : ['score']

details.name: Celsius To Fahrenheit Conversion
details.description: Construct a program that computes the Fahrenheit equivalent of an input Celsius value using the formula F = (9/5)C + 32. The input Celsius value is an integer.

details.name: Fahrenheit to Celsius Conversion
details.description: Construct a program that computes the Celsius equivalent of an input Fahrenheit value using the formula C = (F - 32) (5/9). The input Fahrenheit value is an integer.

details.name: Finding the Maximum Value in a List
details.description: Write a program that finds the maximum value in a list.

details.name: Finding the Minimum Value in a List
details.description: Write a program that finds the minimum value in a list.

details.name: Calculating the Employee's Wage Based on the Hours That the Employee Has Worked and an Hourly Pay Rate
details.description: Construct a program for the payment department of a company to calculate the wage of an employee based on the number of hours that the employee has worked. If an employee works over 40 hours in a week, the payment amount should take into account the overtime hours. The overtime hours are paid at a rate one and a half times the regular pay rate.

details.name: Calculating the Wage of an Employee at the Customer Service Call Center
details.description: Construct a program for the payment department of a company to calculate the wage of an employee who works at the customer service call center. Like other employees in the company, the employees at the customer service call center are paid based on the hours that they work. If they work over 40 hours in a week, the payment amount should take into account the overtime hours. The overtime hours are paid at a rate one and a half times the regular pay rate.\nThe company's policy is to pay more to those employees at the customer service call center who work during weekends. Therefore, the minimum extra pay that the employees could receive for each day of work during weekends is $30. The extra pay increases to the maximum of $50 for the employees who have at least 5 days of work during weekends.
